title: Installing Outdoor Wall Sconce and Recessed Lights: Exterior Wiring and Weatherproofing

locations.name: Exterior entry wall near stairs (probable, outdoors)
locations.basis: Transcript repeatedly references outside, stairs, granite surface, and exterior lighting; no explicit filming location given

summary: This Old House demonstrates upgrading an outdoor lighting setup by removing a poorly mounted exterior fixture, locating and preparing a pancake box embedded in granite, wiring a new wall-sconce with proper hot, neutral, and ground connections, and adding old-work recessed lighting with wet-location LED trims. The segment emphasizes weatherproofing choices (wet-location trims and sealed LED housing) and aesthetic considerations (iron-toned trim and frosted glass) to improve safety, accessibility, and the welcoming feel of the entryway. Safety notes include shutting power off before removing fixtures and ensuring proper mounting to a structural box to prevent water intrusion.
topics: Granite surface preparation for electrical box
Hammer drill and chisel for stone
Weatherproofing and bug prevention for outdoor lights
Aesthetic finishing: iron trim and frosted glass
Entry illumination for safety and welcome

sections.title: Assessment and upgrade planning for exterior lighting
concepts: Planning for proper exterior lighting vs. ad-hoc lighting
sections.description: The hosts note the outside lighting is an afterthought and rush job, discuss the need for a more deliberate exterior lighting plan, and acknowledge the importance of proper mounting and permits when upgrading exterior lighting.

sections.title: Remove old fixture and identify pancake box behind granite
concepts: Identifying a pancake box for outdoor wiring
Wiring junctions between inside and outside fixtures
sections.description: The presenter demonstrates pulling down the old fixture, confirms power is off, and explains that the box behind the wall is a pancake box used to splice interior wiring to the exterior fixture. They note granite depth concerns.

sections.title: Granite modification to accommodate the box
concepts: Plan to trace and chisel granite
sections.description: Attention turns to the granite surface as the intended mounting area. The plan is to trace the box location, then use a hammer drill and chisel to remove granite and set it in place as needed for mounting depth.

sections.title: Exterior wall sconce installation: mounting and wiring
sections.description: The light fixture is chosen for its iron finish and frosted glass. The bracket attaches to the box, and the wires are connected (white = neutral, black = hot, with a ground). The fixture is mounted and prepared for operation.

sections.title: Recessed lighting installation and wet-location trim
concepts: Cutting a hole and mounting a junction box
Drywall clips to hold the housing
Wet-location LED trim for outdoor use
sections.description: The presenter introduces an old-work recessed can, explains how a cut hole leads to a junction box with spliced wires, and demonstrates drywall clips that clamp the fixture in place. Because the installation is outdoors, a wet-location LED trim is used to seal against moisture and bugs.

sections.title: Test and final impression
concepts: Aesthetic and welcoming effect of proper exterior lighting
sections.description: With the lights on, the entry looks significantly more welcoming and well-lit, concluding the demonstration.
